title: kv: holistic residency controller and adaptive page trimmer
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: High-client-load experiments revealed that large sparse allocations and partial page lifetimes were driving elevated fragmentation and increasing spill pressure during bursty workloads. Existing eviction heuristics were reactive and operated at a per-slot granularity, which produced noisy eviction churn and tail latency spikes under multi-tenant mixes. This PR introduces a holistic 'residency controller' to reason about page residency at page and tenant scopes, plus an adaptive background 'page trimmer' that safely collapses underutilized partial pages to improve compactness without synchronous eviction storms.

What this changes (high level): residency controller: computes a composite residency_score per page combining: occupancy_ratio, fragmentation_factor, recent_access_weight (LFU window), tenant_priority, and bounce_rate (re-pinned after trim). Scores drive eviction preference buckets (hot/warm/cold) and per-tenant soft quotas. The controller emits new metrics and exposes a dynamic evictor hook for policy experiments. page trimmer: background worker that periodically scans low-residency candidates and atomically compacts live slots into contiguous pages, freeing trailing partial pages. The trimmer uses adaptive pacing based on in-flight IO, KV writeback pressure, and a conservative max_trims_per_cycle derived from observed latency erosion. Trimming is strictly cooperative: if eviction/backpressure signals are active the trimmer backs off.

Implementation notes: - residency controller implemented in src/kv/residency_controller.rs; algorithm heavily commented and isolated behind a feature gate. - page trimmer implemented in src/kv/page_trimmer.cc with a small shim in src/kv/trimmer_adapter.go to integrate with the Go runtime scheduler used by the server. - New on-disk page metadata version bump (+migration path) is transparent: a lightweight upgrade path migrates metadata lazily during trimmer runs; no offline migration required. - Metrics added: kv.residency.score, kv.page.trim.count, kv.page.trim.latency_ms, kv.fragmentation.p50/p90, kv.residency.evictions_by_bucket. - Admin flags in config: kv.residency.enabled, kv.residency.safe_mode (start with safe heuristics), kv.trimmer.max_ops_per_cycle, kv.trimmer.backoff_threshold.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests and property tests validate score monotonicity and that trimming never drops live key references. Integration test harness simulates tenant mixes with skewed hot keys and short-lived bursts. Microbenchmarks against the existing master show: 6.1% reduction in average working set size for mixed tenant workloads, 9% reduction in total spill bytes during bursty tails, and 3–7% improvement in p99 generation latency under sustained heavy load when safe_mode=false. CI: flaky kernel binding test failed on first run (linux-kernel-bind-check) but was rerun and passed; full CI green at merge.

Migration and rollout plan: feature gated off by default (kv.residency.enabled=false). Staged rollout: canary in Dedicated -> monitor kv.fragmentation.* and kv.page.trim.*; enable safe_mode=true for first 48h, then safe_mode=false if metrics stable. Rollback: disable kv.residency.enabled.

Risks and mitigations: trimming is IO-intensive if misconfigured; mitigated by dynamic pacing and backpressure signals from the IO path. Potential for eviction policy regressions on pathological synthetic workloads; mitigated by A/B experiments, and the residency controller ships with a tunable decay window and conservative default thresholds.

Related: ENG-1719 (fragmentation telemetry), ENG-1802 (tenant-aware eviction).

review_comments: Ethan Russo: Nice isolation of the score computation. Question: have you tried moving the bounce_rate into the decay term instead of the score? Might stabilize churn.

Priya Nair: considered that; we experimented and found it made hot->cold transitions too slow for our bursty demos. Leaving bounce_rate as a penalty in the score gives more direct control and is easier to expose for tuning.
Marisol Ortega: request: add a knob to cap memory reclaimed per second to limit latency impact during compaction cycles.
Priya Nair: added kv.trimmer.max_ops_per_cycle and pacing; documented the knob and default in config/defaults.yaml.
Liam Patel: CI hit on linux-kernel-bind-check; looks unrelated but please re-run. Also add a short section in ops docs about rollout signals.
Priya Nair: re-ran CI, fixed a race in the mmap path that surfaced on the kernel-bind CI node, added docs/ops/kv-residency.md with rollout guidance.
Marisol Ortega: approving after documentation and the pacing knob were added.
Ethan Russo: approved - perf numbers look reasonable; recommend canary and 72h observation window for Dedicated.
release_notes: Introduce residency controller and adaptive page trimmer to reduce KV cache fragmentation, reduce spill bytes under bursty load, and improve tail latency. Feature gated and off by default; can be enabled via kv.residency.enabled and configured via kv.trimmer.* flags.
